title: Polenta con Funghi Porcini
subtitle: Soft polenta with porcini mushroom sauce
excerpt: Polenta con funghi porcini is soft, creamy polenta served with a rich sauce of reconstituted dried porcini and fresh mushrooms in white wine and tomato. It is an autumn dish of the Italian Alps and Apennines, where porcini are abundant and polenta is the staple grain.
sourceNotes: Polenta with porcini is a traditional dish of northern Italy and the Alpine foothills. Polenta has been the staple food of northern Italy since maize arrived from the Americas in the sixteenth century. Porcini mushrooms are gathered from Alpine forests in September and October.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The mushroom sauce can be made a day ahead.

content.text: Traditional polenta requires 45 minutes of stirring, which builds the flavour and gives the correct creamy texture. Instant polenta takes 5 minutes but tastes noticeably less good. For the mushroom sauce, strain the porcini soaking liquid carefully through a fine sieve -- it is full of earthy flavour but also fine grit that must be removed.

items.prepNote: soaked in 300ml just-boiled water for 20 minutes, strained (soaking liquid reserved)

content.text: Soak {{mushrooms-porcini-dried}} porcini in just-boiled water for 20 minutes. Strain the liquid through a fine sieve and reserve. Chop the porcini roughly.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} olive oil in a frying pan over high heat. Fry {{mushrooms-chestnut}} chestnut mushrooms in batches until golden. Add the porcini. Reduce the heat to medium, add {{onion}} onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{thyme-fresh}} thyme (if using). Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and let bubble. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes and the porcini soaking liquid. Simmer for 20 minutes until rich.

Bring 1 litre of water and {{whole-milk}} milk to a boil with {{salt-table}} salt. Pour in {{polenta}} polenta in a thin stream, stirring constantly. Reduce to a very low simmer and stir every few minutes for 40 to 45 minutes until thick and the polenta pulls away from the sides. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} butter and {{parmesan}} Parmesan.
Serve the polenta in wide bowls with the mushroom sauce spooned generously over the top.

items.cause: The polenta was added too quickly or the liquid was not hot enough.
items.fix: Pour polenta into boiling liquid in a thin, slow stream while whisking constantly. Once all the polenta is in, switch to a wooden spoon and stir regularly. Lumps form if the polenta hits cold liquid.

content.text: Polenta with mushrooms is a classic of the Italian Alps, from Piedmont through Lombardy and the Veneto. In these regions polenta was the staple starch for several centuries. It remains a central part of the autumn and winter diet. Porcini are gathered from forest clearings between August and November. They are the most important wild mushroom in northern Italy and the best match for polenta.
